name: Joaquín Torres

summary: Joaquín Torres was born in Mexico and was six when he crossed into the United States with his mother and grandmother, growing up in Sonoita, Arizona, and finishing high school on the honor roll. He never forgot the people still trying to make the crossing, and he made a habit of leaving water, food and medicine along the border for them. That habit put him in the path of the Sons of the Serpent, who were snatching people at the border and delivering them to the rogue scientist Karl Malus for experiments.

When Joaquín vanished, his grandmother Mariana turned to Sam Wilson, then serving as Captain America. Sam tracked the trail to Malus's base in New York and found that Joaquín had been rebuilt into a human-falcon hybrid using DNA from Redwing, Sam's own bird partner. Malus's other subjects changed back once rescued; Joaquín did not. Claire Temple worked out why: Redwing carried a vampiric strain, and it had left Joaquín with a healing factor that kept the transformation locked in place.

The change also tied him into Redwing's psychic link with Sam. When Serpent Society thugs hurled Captain America off a building, Joaquín heard the alarm through that link and caught him in mid-air, then held his own against the Serpents with Sam feeding him moves through Redwing. Afterward he took up the Falcon name as Cap's partner. He first appeared only in a photograph in issue #1 (December 2015), made his full debut in #3 (January 2016) and wore the Falcon identity from #6 (April 2016); the wiki credits Nick Spencer and Daniel Acuña as his creators.

comics.title: A New Falcon Takes Flight
comics.summary: Kidnapped by the Sons of the Serpent and remade by Karl Malus with Redwing's DNA, Joaquín became a permanent human-falcon hybrid with wings grown from his arms and a healing factor inherited from Redwing's vampiric strain. Sharing Redwing's mental link with Sam Wilson, he saved Captain America from a deadly fall and helped beat the Serpent Society. By the end of the opening arc he had claimed the Falcon name as Sam's partner.

comics.title: Captain America's Partner
comics.summary: Joaquín stayed at Sam's side through the rest of Captain America: Sam Wilson. One story in issue #17 shows him rescuing Ariella Conner, a divisive political figure, when she is attacked during a university speech. Conner had previously called for him to be deported, and she promptly spun the rescue to serve her own agenda.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom: Captain America: Sam Wilson Vol 1 17

comics.title: The Underground
comics.summary: When Hydra seized control of the United States, Joaquín joined the Underground resistance working against the new regime. He operated alongside members of the Champions as well as Ironheart and the Wasp, and the event's first issue features him among the young heroes of the resistance.

comics.title: Back in Sam's Orbit
comics.summary: When Sam Wilson returned to the Falcon identity in his own series, Joaquín remained in the supporting cast, still credited as Falcon himself. In one issue the new Patriot, Rayshaun Lucas, teased him with a list of joke codenames now that the name was shared.

comics.title: Teen Hero on the Roster
comics.summary: Joaquín was a featured member of the Champions when the team's 2019 series launched. In the 2020 Outlawed crisis, as the government moved against teenage heroes, he insisted the Champions could stand on their own, only to be reminded by a senator that he had been trained by Sam Wilson. Under the new rules he signed on to be mentored by Sam Wilson.

comics.title: Supporting Sam's Shield
comics.summary: With Sam carrying the shield again in Captain America: Symbol of Truth, Joaquín returned as a recurring supporting character, credited in issues across the run from #1 to #14. The opening issue also introduced his cousin Luísa.

comics.title: Better Angels
comics.summary: The private military firm Eaglestar International abducted Joaquín and harvested his DNA aboard Skydream, a floating platform, to create winged guards called the War Angels. Broken out by Shadow Soldier (Josiah X) and later teamed with Sam and Sam's cousin Billie, he fought through the platform alongside Patriot (Elijah Bradley) and the Red Hulk, helped shut down its weapons before the fleet could strike cities with large Black populations, and then helped hand out Skydream's resources to the people it had hurt.

screen.title: The Falcon and The Winter Soldier
screen.summary: A U.S. Air Force officer who looks up to Sam Wilson, Torres backs Sam from the ground during a rescue mission in North Africa, is the first to warn him about the Flag Smashers, and gets knocked out after stumbling into one of their bank robberies in Switzerland. Across five of the six episodes (by voice only in episode 3), he flies Sam and Bucky Barnes to Germany and, in episode 5, is handed the Falcon wings by Sam.

sources.label: MCU Wiki: The Falcon and The Winter Soldier

screen.title: Captain America: Brave New World
screen.summary: Now flying as the new Falcon in Sam's restored old wings, Torres helps stop SERPENT's sale of stolen adamantium in Mexico, meets Isaiah Bradley, and works the investigation after an attack on President Ross at the White House. He and Sam uncover the Leader's mind-control scheme at Camp Echo One, and he writes a program to block its trigger. Shot down near Celestial Island while destroying a missile, he survives surgery, and Sam tells him to be ready for a rebuilt Avengers.

sources.label: MCU Wiki: Captain America: Brave New World

trivia.fact: His healing factor is strong enough that he came back from a fatal wound after the Serpent Society's Cottonmouth bit his head.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom: Captain America: Sam Wilson Vol 1 6

trivia.fact: He was seventeen years old at the time of Captain America: Sam Wilson #5 (2016).

sources.label: Marvel Fandom: Captain America: Sam Wilson Vol 1 5

trivia.fact: After Sam reclaimed the Falcon name, Patriot (Rayshaun Lucas) jokingly offered Joaquín replacement codenames such as Squawkman.

The screen version is a different man from the comics one: the MCU Torres grew up in Miami and serves in the Air Force's 547th Intelligence Squadron at Nellis Air Force Base, while the comics Joaquín was born in Mexico and raised in Arizona.

His MCU military rank: the MCU Wiki character page gives Captain, while the Brave New World film page calls him Lieutenant, so no rank is stated.
